summary: The business behind Tanishq jewellery, Titan and Fastrack watches, Titan Eye+ eyewear and other lifestyle products.
description: Titan makes or arranges products and sells them through shops and online. For example, a wedding shopper may buy a Tanishq necklace, while another customer buys spectacles at Titan Eye+. These purchases need different materials, staff and services, even though they belong to one group.
money: Customers pay for jewellery, watches, spectacles and other products. Titan must pay for materials or finished goods, making products, shop staff, rent, advertising and running the business. It also needs money to keep unsold products in its shops. The whole customer bill is not profit.
customers: People buying jewellery, gifts, watches, spectacles, clothing, fragrances or bags. Some outlets are operated by business partners, so the route by which Titan receives payment can differ between shops.
drivers: How much customers buy, what they choose, gold and other material costs, discounts, shop costs and how long products wait before being sold.

groups.title: Jewellery
groups.examples: Tanishq, Mia, Zoya, CaratLane and the acquired Damas business.
groups.explanation: A necklace buyer pays for metal, stones, design and making the item. If gold becomes dearer, the same weight of gold can produce a larger bill. That does not by itself mean Titan sold more jewellery.

groups.title: Watches and wearables
groups.examples: Titan, Fastrack, Sonata, smart wearables and watch shops such as Helios.
groups.explanation: Customers choose a watch for its appearance, features, brand and price. A traditional watch with hands and a smart wearable need different components and face different competing products.

groups.title: Spectacles and eyecare retail
groups.examples: Titan Eye+ frames, lenses and related optical services.
groups.explanation: A shopper chooses frames and suitable lenses, with help from store staff and the services offered. Titan must cover the product and shop-service costs. This description does not assess medical outcomes.

groups.title: Other lifestyle products
groups.examples: Taneira clothing, SKINN fragrances and IRTH bags.
groups.explanation: These products serve different shopping needs from jewellery. Each range needs stock, staff and promotion; using a familiar group name does not guarantee that it earns a profit.

basics.title: A brand and a business group are different
basics.text: Tanishq is a brand. Jewellery is the wider reporting group that includes several brands and activities. The accounts combine controlled companies under the reporting rules. A Jewellery result therefore does not tell us the profit on one Tanishq ring.

basics.title: A branded shop is not always owned and run in the same way
basics.text: Some shops are run by Titan and others through franchise arrangements: another business operates a branded outlet under agreed terms. More shops means more places to reach customers, but does not mean Titan owns every building or pays identical costs at each outlet.

steps.title: Choose products people want to buy
steps.text: Decide which designs, sizes and prices to offer for weddings, gifts and everyday use.

steps.title: Arrange the goods and check their quality
steps.text: Obtain metal, stones, watch parts or finished goods and arrange the making and quality checks needed for each range.

steps.title: Put products where shoppers can find them
steps.text: Supply shops and online orders. Unsold jewellery and other goods still need funding and storage.

steps.title: Sell, receive payment and provide promised support
steps.text: The customer pays for the purchase. Titan must cover the associated costs and any promised exchanges, repairs or other support afterwards.

specifics.title: A larger jewellery bill can have several causes
specifics.text: Sales can rise because gold prices rose, more people bought, purchases were larger, or customers chose different stones and designs. Making charges are not pure profit: they also have to cover the cost of making and selling the item.

specifics.title: Gold in a shop needs money before it sells
specifics.text: Stock means goods held for sale. Titan can use borrowing and gold-loan arrangements to obtain that stock. A gold loan here can mean borrowing the metal itself for the business, rather than a customer borrowing cash against jewellery. Hedging means arrangements to limit particular price changes. It does not remove borrowing costs or guarantee that customers will buy.

specifics.title: New shops and different products change costs
specifics.text: A new shop can need time to attract regular buyers while rent and staff costs begin immediately. Plain-gold jewellery and jewellery with stones also have different costs. Check what is selling and which shops have been open long enough for a fair comparison.

watch: Are jewellery sales rising because people buy more, or because gold costs more?
The sales value alone cannot answer this.
Read the company’s measures of buyers, purchases and weight sold where available. Compare the same periods. Customers may buy lighter items when gold becomes dearer.
Which products are helping or hurting earnings?
Different jewellery and watches have different costs.
Read changes in plain-gold versus stone-set jewellery, traditional watches and wearables. Check discounts, materials and advertising rather than guessing profit from the selling price.
Jewellery can tie up money before a customer buys it.
Read stock, borrowing, gold-loan and price-protection notes together. Check when repayments are due and which price risks remain.
Do newer shops cover their costs?
Opening a shop and earning a return are different achievements.
Compare older shops with newer ones where disclosed, and read rent, staff, stock and investment needs. Check Watches, Eyecare and newer categories separately.
Are we comparing the same businesses and sales definitions?
An acquisition or a changed definition can raise a reported total.

The cited annual presentation includes Damas after its acquisition and removes bullion and digi-gold from some headline figures. Bullion means gold sold as metal rather than finished jewellery; digi-gold involves buying gold through a digital service rather than buying a finished jewellery item. Use the same business boundary and definition when comparing years.
risks: Dearer gold can require more money for shop stock and lead customers to buy lighter items or postpone purchases.
Purity, product quality, repairs and the buying experience matter. Investigate which products or shops a reported problem affects.
Expansion costs more than it earns
New shops, product ranges or acquired businesses can need staff, stock and investment before enough customers arrive.
Local jewellers, national brands and online sellers compete on price, design and service; watches and eyewear face their own alternatives.
context: November 2026: a one-off gold tax gain lifted profit

Titan’s 5 November 2026 results for July–September 2026 say income rose by a quarter and reported profit before tax rose by about half compared with a year earlier. Part of that profit was a one-off gain that Titan links to a rise in the customs duty (the import tax) on gold. Without that gain, profit before tax rose 18 per cent. Its earlier 6 October update said the number of jewellery buyers grew only in the mid-single digits, while the average bill grew by double digits. The international figures include Damas, a Gulf jewellery business two-thirds owned by Titan and included in its accounts since January 2026.

financialNotes.title: The watch name does not describe the largest earnings source
financialNotes.text: In the verified FY 2025–26 consolidated segment statement, Jewellery reports ₹79,660 crore of revenue and ₹7,209 crore segment profit; Watches reports ₹5,267 crore and ₹824 crore respectively. These are segment measures before company-level finance costs, exceptional items and tax, not individual-brand profits.

financialNotes.title: Check which gold sales the headline includes
financialNotes.text: The statutory table includes other income, bullion and digi-gold sales. The earnings presentation excludes bullion and digi-gold from specified headline total-income figures. These different definitions should not be treated as conflicting versions of the same sales measure or mixed to calculate a margin.

financialNotes.title: Keep corporate costs and cash in view
financialNotes.text: The corporate unallocated line has a ₹201 crore loss, reducing the combined segment result. The Others row is not a profit measure for every new lifestyle brand. Read the reconciliation, inventory funding, acquisition payments and cash flow before treating the segment total as cash available to shareholders.

stepsTitle: From the workshop to the shop counter.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: Titan sells Tanishq jewellery, Titan and Fastrack watches, Titan Eye+ glasses and other lifestyle products.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Shoppers buying jewellery, gifts, watches, glasses, clothing, fragrances or bags. Some shops are run by business partners, so payment can reach Titan by different routes.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: Customers pay for the products. For jewellery, the bill includes the gold and stones and a making charge.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Gold and other materials or finished goods, making products, shop staff, rent, advertising, and money to keep stock in shops.

helps.title: Well-known brands
helps.text: Tanishq, Titan, Fastrack and Titan Eye+ are separate brands for jewellery, watches and glasses, each with its own shops, so shoppers can recognise what they are buying.

helps.title: Protection from gold price swings
helps.text: Titan’s FY 2025–26 annual report says it borrows gold from banks and fixes the gold price only when a customer buys the jewellery. It also uses hedges, contracts that limit the effect of price changes, so a sudden move in gold prices hurts less.

helps.title: New shops add reach
helps.text: Each new shop puts Titan’s products in front of more shoppers once it attracts regular buyers. Titan keeps opening shops; it added 78, after closures, in July–September 2026.

hurts.title: Gold prices swing
hurts.text: Titan’s annual report says global conflicts make gold prices and currencies unstable, which can change how much shoppers spend. Dearer gold also needs more money to keep shop stock, and buyers may choose lighter pieces or wait.

hurts.title: Tax on gold can change
hurts.text: The annual report says jewellery is sensitive to changes in the import tax (customs duty) on gold, which change Titan’s costs, prices and demand.

hurts.title: Strong competitors
hurts.text: Local jewellers, national brands and online sellers compete on price, design and service. Titan’s annual report notes growing competition for CaratLane and heightened competition in cheaper watches.
